passes.notes: Both answers handle the outage and the partial day honestly. A uses a clean shaded 'No data' band, a hatched bar marked 41* for Mar 21, and a plain note that excludes Mar 21 from the average and says it shouldn't be read as the highest day. B labels Mar 21 'morning only' right at the point and adds a useful data table, but its gap label collides with a gridline ('Mar 9–11' is struck through) and the shaded band spills over the Mar 8 and Mar 12 points, so it looks less polished for a staff email.

Both answers show Mar 9–11 as a shaded no-data gap and mark Mar 21 as morning only. B's bars are cleaner: the hatched Mar 21 bar comes with a legend note saying it isn't comparable and was left out of the average. A's line chart has overlapping text in the gap label ('No data' collides with 'Mar 9–11'). Its dashed segment also still draws a rising line up to the partial 41, though A does add a helpful data table.
